findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine tested at 0 ppm of chlorine. Repair the machine to operate according to manufacturer’s specifications. It is difficult to know the specifications with out a data plate. There is a plastic sticker on the machine that states wash and rinse shall be a minimum of 120F. The machine is reading approximately 110F on the gauge and the water in the machine is 104F with a probe directly after a cycle has been run. Do not use the dish machine until it is repaired to function according to manufacturer’s specifications so that it sanitizes properly. A chart can be found in the code section listed below. The information in the following code reference is an example. P139 2017 FDA food code. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.120, 250 & 151 - A) 1. Squeeze bottles of dressing in metal containers on an ice bath at the lunch buffet had surface temperatures above 50F for portions not in contact with ice. The bottom of the containers had surface temperatures of 41f/below. The internal temperature of blue cheese was 58F-60F. Dressings were discarded at the end of lunch buffet service period (11a-3p). Discussed adequate ice bath for maintaining dressings at 41F/below or use of time control for dressings on lunch buffet.
2. Lite Ranch dressing in bottom of sandwich cooler had surface and internal temperatures of 56F and 58F. GM noted the dressing was out during lunch period. Dressing was discarded in trash. Labeling states "keep refrigerated". Keep the dressing in the cooler, get it out as needed, and immediately place the product back in the cooler for storage. Otherwise, get out a smaller portion and use time control for lunch/dinner hours (use/discard w/in 4hrs).

B) Container of cheese sauce being used to make pizzas was out at the pizza cooler upon arrival of inspector. Surface temperature of portion was at 59F. Staff stated it was out for ~45 minutes. Very small amount was left. Cheese sauce was discarded and replaced with fresh product.

Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be held at 41F/below at all times during storage, use and while on display. Maintain cold PHF at 41F/below or establish and adhere to a time control policy. If time control is used then foods must be used or discarded w/in 4hrs and cannot go back in cold storage after being out at ambient temperature for use.

C) Date marking of foods was inconsistent. Some products had day dots with dates written on them, and some foods just had day dots with the day of the week on them. Ham had a prep date, and sausage was observed without any date mark at all. Gm stated foods are supposed to be labeled with the date of discard on the day dots. Benefit of doubt was given for foods based on information provided. Foods were kept and dated for use. 

Refrigerated potentially hazardous foods shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
**NOTE: The date marking system needs to be tweaked so it is clearly understood and done consistently the same by all staff. (see general comments)**

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation

B) Pitchers of dressings and a pan of lettuce were uncovered in the reach-in salad cooler. Cover foods between uses/during storage.

750.510 - A) Employee working cash register did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to slice pizza.

B) Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique.

Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed during inspection (educational handouts provided)
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changed, and prior to handling food, clean equipment or unwrapped single service items.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A) (R) Mold was observed inside the ice machine on the front and sides of the white baffle. The gash observed to have heavy mold accumulation during the previous inspection had slight mold buildup and still needed to be repaired. Other small pits were also observed. Clean and sanitize the baffle as needed. Make necessary repairs to eliminate gashes/pits. If repairs can not be made to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface then replace the baffle.

B) (R) Containers and lids were observed to be cracked and broken. Replace cracked/broken containers and lids.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Previously used, disposable wiping cloths were observed stored with spray bottles of sanitizer, orange force cleaner, and glass cleaner. Wiping cloths used with sanitizer musts be discarded after each use. Otherwise, wiping cloths must be stored in a bucket with sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms.

Throw away disposable wiping cloths after use or change to sani-bucket storage and store wet wiping cloths in solution between uses.
 Moist wiping cloths used for wiping general surfaces such as dining tables, counters, etc. must be cleaned and rinsed as specified in Section 750.810(b) and used for no other purpose. the cloths shall be stored in sanitize solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b  - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) slicers - at pizza window (grease/food debris);   and
B) dish machine - inside doors (grease/debris).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
In-use equipment and utensils (i.e. slicers, knives, can opener, etc.) must go through ware washing process up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
. 750.880 - A) (R) Toothpicks at sandwich cooler were observed with frilled and food contact surfaces intermixed in the storage box. Store toothpicks in a manner that will allow for only the frilled ends to be handled when being retrieved for use.

B) (R) Plastic utensils in storage tubs were observed with food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. Store utensils all facing once direction so only handles will be touched when utensils are retrieved for use.

C) 1. Utensil storage container at pizza service window was soiled with food crumbs/debris.
2. Storage containers for sauce cups and lids on top of sandwich cooler were soiled with dust and food debris.
Clean storage containers daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

D) 1. To go boxes at front counter were stored with the food contact surface up.
2. Sauce cups in container on top of sandwich cooler stored with the food contact surface up. 

E) Single use gloves were observed out and stored in a box with single use coffee packets. Leave gloves in the original box or in a clean, sealed food grade container.

Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Keep single service covered in storage areas.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1130(e) - Containers with stagnant, old moldy water was observed under plumbing at the 3 part sink and in the cabinet below the soda machine. Pans were emptied and cleaned during the inspection If leaks are present then have leaks properly repaired. Until leaks are repaired, empty and clean pans used to catch leaking water daily/as needed. Old, stagnant water is water and can serve as a food/water source for pests.

Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) (R)  Floor under/behind the ice machine was soiled with dust, debris, and a dirty food container.

B) (R) Floor drain cover under ice machine and sandwich cooler was soiled with mold/debris.

C) Floor under sandwich cooler was soiled with food/general debris.

D) Floor drains under sprayer sink and behind drink counter were soiled with mold buildup.

Floors and drains shall be maintained clean. Clean floors and drains daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.130 - The following were observed without proper labels:
A) seasoning shakers at sandwich cooler;   and
B) pizza dough yeast in bulk food bin.

Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the original packaging shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Several foods were observed without date marks or with date marks that indicated products were past the 7 day time frame for use.
Foods included hotdogs in the dough cooler (no date on one bag; date of 10/26 on another bag); cheese sauce in the bottom of pizza cooler (no date on container or squeeze bottle); macaroni noodles in bottom of pizza cooler (no date on one container; date of 11/26 on another container). Foods were discarded in the trash.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous foods shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
**NOTE: some day dots had dates for discard and some did not. Other items had dates noted on bags with no day of the week indicated. The date marking system needs to be tweaked so it is clearly understood and done consistently the same by all staff.**

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - (R) Ice cream chest freezer did not have a thermometer inside. Provide a thermometer for the freezer.
GM provided a thermometer during the inspection.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Sealed packages of cheese sauce and pre-cooked macaroni noodles were observed in the basin of the 3 part sink. Closing manager stated items are pulled from the freezer and usually thawed in standing water. Manager was unsure as to how long items were thawing in the sink and stated they could have been in there since 11a. It was after 2p. Internal temperatures were checked. Noodles were at 39F-45F. Noodles were placed in a clean, covered container, dated, and put in a cooler for storage. Cheese sauce had internal temperature of 52F-55F. Cheese sauce was discarded in the trash. 
Do not thaw potentially hazardous foods in standing water or at ambient temperature for any reason. Preferable method of thawing is under refrigeration - plan ahead and place frozen foods in the walkin cooler to thaw overnight when possible.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under  potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - A) Liquid butter was observed uncovered and not in use at the pizza window.
B) Containers of ranch dressing and cherry tomatoes were uncovered in the salad cooler.

Foods shall be properly stored and protected at all times. Cover foods during slow periods and when they are not in use to protect items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Manager handled her phone and did not wash hands prior to touching the edge of lettuce in the top of sandwich while discussing use/storage practice for the product. Manager stated the top edge of the lettuce is not supposed to be used due to quality purposes. Piece of lettuce was discarded at request of inspector.
 
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.
Never touch any food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service articles without first washing hands, especially after handling unclean items, such as phones and other personal items. Gloves need to be worn in addition to handwashing when ready to eat foods are handled and will not be subject to cooking.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Open bottle of water was observed between the cheese shredder and coffee maker. Personal drink was discarded during the inspection.

Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection. Drinks shall be in a cup with a lid and straw and stored in a manner that will not potentially cause cross contamination of food and food related items (i.e. clean equipment and single service items).

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A) Mold was observed inside the ice machine on the white baffle and on the walls around the baffle. A gash with mold accumulation was also observed on the white baffle. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. Repair the area of disrepair where mold has accumulated and is not easy to clean.

B) Containers and lids were observed to be cracked and broken. Replace cracked/broken containers and lids (i.e. container holding cheese sauce in bottom of pizza cooler; lid on container used to toss foods in sauce at sandwich cooler etc.).

C) Metal pizza spatula (used to retrieve pizzas from the oven) had pieces broken off and crevices along damaged edges. Pizza spatula was discarded in the trash by manager during inspection. 

 Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - (R) Quat test strips were not available for checking sanitizer. Obtain and use quat test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration is maintained at wall dispenser and in spray bottles.
GM provided test strips during inspection.
A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of each chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solutions in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b  - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) slicers - above prep cooler and at pizza window (grease/food debris);
B) knife - sandwich cooler (food debris);  and
C) soda nozzle/diffusers (mold).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
In-use equipment and utensils (i.e. slicers, knives, can opener, etc.) must go through ware washing process up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) trays beneath pizza tray storage (carbon/food debris);
B) shelves in dry storage (sugar on shelves holding cotton candy sugar and register tape);  and
C) drain line under ice machine (mold)

Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - A) (R) Single service utensils were uncovered in storage area. Cover utensils in storage area.

B) Toothpicks at sandwich cooler were observed with frilled and food contact surfaces intermixed in the storage box. Store toothpicks in a manner that will allow for only the frilled ends to be handled when being retrieved for use.

C) To go boxes were stored with food surfaces up at the pizza window. Boxes were inverted to protect food contact surfaces. 

D) 1. Knives were observed within handles and food contact surfaces extended up out of a cup in the dry storage area. 
2. Plastic utensils in storage tubs were observed with food contact surfaces and handles intermixed.
Store utensils in cups with handles presented out. Store all utensils in tubs facing one direction with handles presented out so food contact surfaces are not being touched when utensils are retrieved for use.

E) Roll of garbage bags in storage cabinet beneath salad bar was in direct contact with plastic wrap used to cover foods. Roll of garbage bags was moved so it was no longer in contact with the plastic wrap.

Single-service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user. Keep single service covered in storage areas.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1110 - (R) Restrooms did not have covered waste cans for diaper changing areas. Provide covered waste cans in both restrooms.

Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) 1. Floor under/behind the ice machine was soiled with dust, debris, and a dirty food container.
2. Floor drain cover under ice machine and sandwich cooler was soiled with mold/debris.

B) Floor tiles in front of ice machine had low grout. Areas with low grout were holding water and debris. Re-grout low lying areas to eliminate puddling of water/debris.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. 
NOTE: An odor was present under/around the ice machine. This may have something to do with the mold/debris underneath and on the drain line under the machine (see #23). Clean under/around the ice machine as needed to help minimize debris and presence of odors.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.citation_text:
750.1310 - Canister of furniture polish and unlabeled spray bottles were observed with a spray bottle of water for the salad bar, tongs, and plastic wrap in a cabinet below the salad bar. Spray bottles contained blue liquid (presumed to be glass cleaner) and light pink liquid (sanitizer - tested with quat test strip at 200ppm).
All chemicals were removed from the cabinet; spray bottles were labeled as to the contents.

All toxic items must be properly stored, separate from food and food related items (i.e. clean equipment and single service items) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.
Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Several spray bottles were observed without labels, including quat sanitizer, degreaser, and glass cleaner. Several bottles of quat sanitizer were also improperly labeled as glass cleaner and orange force cleaner. Bottles were properly labeled during the inspection.
Maintain proper labels on bottles and in storage areas for chemicals.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.
